out.rationale: Khan et al. note their expertise gap is only access to information, whereas future models may differ in reasoning. Kenton et al. test closed tasks without information asymmetry and report debate beats consultancy but versus direct QA is mixed: GPT-3.5 benefits (p = 0.037), Pro 1.0 shows no difference and Gemma7B and Pro 1.5 do worse; debaters are still RLHF-tuned, so the honesty-propensity part is not addressed.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether debate's benefit holds when debaters and judge differ in capability rather than information access, for closed QA with LLM judges

out.other_title: Results depend on verified evidence; without a quote tool a liar could invent a narrative
out.rationale: Khan et al. state their results depend on a quote verification tool and expect useful debate to be grounded in verifiable evidence. Kenton et al.'s closed tasks (MMLU, GSM8KQA, PrOntoQA, TruthfulQA, GPQA) have no article for debaters to quote, and there debate beats consultancy but shows small or no benefit over direct QA for the most indicative judges (GPT-3.5 p = 0.037, Pro 1.0 no significant difference); task type and evidence access change together.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether debate helps judges when there is no source text to quote, for closed QA tasks

out.rationale: Leike et al. ask whether debate works beyond fact-checkable statements and whether judges can follow stronger debaters. out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether debate helps weaker judges on questions without verifiable evidence, for closed QA tasks with LLM judges and Gemini Pro 1.5 debaters

text: The paper reports that on closed tasks debate beats consultancy, but against QA without article: Gemma7B does better with direct QA, GPT-3.5 does better with debate (p = 0.037), Pro 1.0 shows no significant difference (p = 0.1), and Pro 1.5, judging debaters of its own model, is worse with debate. The authors read GPT-3.5 and Pro 1.0 as the most indicative of scalable oversight and as showing small or no benefit of debate over direct QA.
title: Closed QA without information asymmetry: debate vs direct QA depends on judge strength
